text: Waterbars are doing their job, tread is in great shape. Paintbrush and lupine everywhere right now.
Out and back before lunch. Icy spots in the trees where the sun never hits, watch your footing. One big downed tree before the junction, well-worn path around it.
A dusting of fresh snow up high, nothing serious yet.
Quick morning lap. Blowdown about two miles in, a short scramble gets you around it. Bring layers, wind picked up at the top.
Solo trip midweek. The switchbacks are greasy after the rain, take it slow coming down.
Late afternoon walk. Sloppy for the first mile, then it dries out nicely. Bring layers, wind picked up at the top.
Sunset hike. Clear and dry the whole way. Take your time on the descent.
Some erosion on the outer edge of the switchbacks, stay inside. Views were worth every step.
Mosquitoes are out in force near the water, bring repellent.
Creek crossings are all rock-hoppable at the moment. Started cold, ended in t-shirts.
Took the kids up. Skeeters bad at dusk, tolerable at midday. Bug pressure is finally easing compared to two weeks ago.
Took the kids up. Trail crew has cleared most of the winter deadfall, nice work. Popular with families on the first mile, thins out fast after that.
The falls are absolutely roaring with runoff.
Loose gravel on the steep pitch, poles recommended. Everything melted out and dried up, prime conditions.
Trail crew has cleared most of the winter deadfall, nice work. Views were worth every step.
Took the kids up. The falls are absolutely roaring with runoff.
Parking lot was full by 8am, arrive early. Take your time on the descent.
One big downed tree before the junction, well-worn path around it.
Deep mud where the horses have churned things up.
Dusty in the exposed sections but otherwise perfect. Started cold, ended in t-shirts.
Icy spots in the trees where the sun never hits, watch your footing.
Boots got heavy in the meadow section, otherwise fine. Wildflowers are going off in the meadows, worth the trip alone.
Did an early start. Seasonal streams mostly dry, carry more water than you think.
The avalanche chutes are green and full of glacier lilies.
Muddy in the usual low spots, gaiters not a bad idea. Sunscreen is non-negotiable up there.
Boots got heavy in the meadow section, otherwise fine.
Water levels dropping, the ford is only shin deep now. The switchbacks are greasy after the rain, take it slow coming down.
Frost on the boardwalks first thing in the morning, slick as glass.
Icy spots in the trees where the sun never hits, watch your footing.
Best conditions I've seen this trail in.
Muddy in the usual low spots, gaiters not a bad idea. Balsamroot blooming along the upper half. Would do it again tomorrow.
Deer flies chased us for a solid mile in the open stretch. Spray from the cascade keeps the lower trail damp all day.
The footbridge over the gorge is completely gone. Creek is raging and there is no safe way across, we turned back.
Bridge washed out about two miles in after last night's storm. Had to turn around, really disappointing.
Crossing at the gorge is impassable, do not attempt. The whole span went downstream, only the far abutment is left standing.
Heads up: the bridge is OUT. Water is still high and fast. A ranger at the trailhead was telling people the trail effectively ends at the creek.
Confirmed the washout everyone is posting about. Wreckage of the old footbridge is wedged against the rocks a hundred yards down. Turn around point for now.
Bridge is still out at the gorge. Rangers say no repair timeline yet, so plan on an out-and-back to the crossing.
FYI the washed-out crossing has NOT been fixed. Saw a couple of people fording at low water but it looked sketchy, would not recommend.
Trail is lovely as far as the creek, but with the bridge gone that is where the trip ends. Sign at the trailhead now says closed beyond mile 2.
